campaign_spec.objective: Prove the pure presence-classification semantics of the new durable-actor profile model (src/core/actor-presence.ts) at the current GPTQueue tree, offline, through one bounded read-only focused vitest run, without any live Redis, MCP, runtime-launch, or task-completion claims.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes passing cases asserting 'active' for a leased processing runtime, 'idle' for a leased idle runtime, and that a leaseless runtime observation is ignored by classification.
requirements.statement: A runtime incarnation holding a lease classifies as 'active' when its workload is 'processing' and 'idle' when its workload is 'idle'; a runtime observation without a lease_id is ignored by classification and does not count as usable presence.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes a passing case asserting that the presence model and classification results carry no per-task delivery-mode field and are unaffected by queued-work state.
requirements.statement: Delivery mode (store_only on a queued task) is a per-task property that is intentionally absent from the presence model, while activation policy is an actor-owned property; presence classification never inspects queued work.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes a passing case asserting presence 'offline_launchable' for a runnable contract with a wake_if_offline policy.
requirements.statement: An offline actor with a runnable launch contract and activation_policy.mode 'wake_if_offline' classifies as 'offline_launchable'.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes a passing case asserting presence 'offline_store_only' for a runnable contract with a store_only policy.
requirements.statement: An offline actor with a runnable launch contract and activation_policy.mode 'store_only' classifies as 'offline_store_only'.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes passing cases exercising the precedence order: leased runtime with an outstanding wake lease still classifies active/idle, a wake lease with a not_runnable contract still classifies 'starting', and offline classification applies only when neither is present.
requirements.statement: Situation precedence holds exactly as implemented in resolveSituation/classifySituation: (1) a leased runtime wins over any wake lease and over offline classification; (2) an outstanding wake lease wins over offline classification; (3) only otherwise is the actor offline, where a non-runnable contract yields 'unavailable' regardless of policy.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes passing cases for each admission error code and passing cases asserting the admitted profile is deeply frozen (mutation attempts do not alter the admitted profile or its nested capabilities/activation_policy).
requirements.statement: admitActorProfile validates identity (non-empty actor_id and alias), activation policy mode ('wake_if_offline' or 'store_only'), and integer max_concurrency >= 1, returning frozen typed errors 'invalid_identity', 'invalid_policy', or 'invalid_concurrency'; an admitted profile is deeply frozen and its capabilities and activation_policy are immutable.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes a passing case asserting presence 'starting' when wake_lease_id is set and no leased runtime is observed.
requirements.statement: An actor with no leased runtime but an outstanding controller-issued wake lease classifies as 'starting'.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes passing cases asserting presence 'unavailable' for a not_runnable contract under both wake_if_offline and store_only policies.
requirements.statement: An offline actor with a not_runnable launch contract classifies as 'unavailable' regardless of activation policy.

acceptance: The controller-observed focused vitest run of tests/actor-presence.test.ts includes a passing case asserting that classifyPresence with an undefined actor returns ok:false with error.code 'unknown_recipient', and that no queue/mailbox/directory data is created.
requirements.statement: classifyPresence rejects an unknown recipient (undefined actor profile) with a frozen { ok: false, error.code: 'unknown_recipient' } classification and creates no queue, mailbox, or directory data.
